digest.en: Serbia's student movement stunned the political establishment, forcing a pivot toward EU integration and away from Vucic's Russia-friendly stance. Simultaneously, Saudi Arabia seeks Chinese missile defense systems to counter Houthi attacks, signaling a shift in Gulf security dependencies.
digest.hi: ईरान ने संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद में अमेरिकी-इज़राइली बलों पर युद्ध अपराध का आरोप लगाया, 254 मौतों की तस्वीरें पेश कीं। इसी दौरान इज़राइल के प्रधानमंत्री नेतन्याहू ने राष्ट्रीय गठबंधन को 56 सीटों के साथ मजबूत किया, जिससे अंतरराष्ट्रीय दबाव में नई जटिलता आई।

articles.title: Tennis great Novak Djokovic praises Serbia's student movement after stunning election win
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic praised Serbia's student-led opposition movement after Aleksander Vucic conceded defeat on October 25. The tennis star said the youth coalition fostered national pride both domestically and abroad. This marked a significant political shift in the region. Aleksander Vucic conceded defeat to a student-led opposition movement on October 25; Novak Djokovic says, the youth movement managed to create a sense of pride in all the people, not just in Serbia but abroad as well.

articles.title: Under Houthi fire, Saudi Arabia looks to China for missile support
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia is expanding a ballistic missile factory near al-Duwadimi to produce longer-range weapons. The facility sits 200 kilometers west of Riyadh. The move aims to bolster strategic deterrence against Houthi attacks. Media reports confirm the shift toward heavier payload capabilities. Saudi Arabia’s rapid expansion of a ballistic missile factory signals a transformative shift in its pursuit of strategic deterrence.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro flees Brazil after presidential election loss, reports say
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro fled Brazil following his presidential election loss to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. He crossed into Argentina before boarding a private plane to Ecuador. Lula called the departure shameful. The senator is reportedly en route to the United States. Far-right senator and his family boarded private plane to Ecuador after crossing border to Argentina, Argentina’s government confirmsThe far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro has reportedly fled Brazil and is on his way to the United States after losing Sunday’s presidential election to the leftwing incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who called the act “shameful”. articles.title: In Myanmar's ancient Bagan, artisans struggling to preserve heritage pin hopes on tourism revival
articles.summary: Artisans in Myanmar's Bagan are struggling to preserve heritage crafts as tourism declines. The civil conflict has reduced international visitors to the UNESCO site. Local communities face threats to their livelihoods and centuries-old traditions. They now pin hopes on a future tourism revival. Once a magnet for international visitors, the UNESCO World Heritage Site is struggling to regain its tourism industry as Myanmar's civil conflict drags on.

articles.title: Federal Reserve likely to skip rate hike despite elevated inflation
articles.summary: The Federal Reserve is likely to skip a rate hike despite elevated inflation. Chairman Kevin Warsh aims to return inflation to the 2% target. Higher borrowing costs typically cool spending and slow price increases. The central bank is weighing its next move carefully. The Fed, led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, wants to return inflation to its 2% target, which it typically does by raising its short-term interest rate.

articles.title: South Korea’s rich lobbying spree isn’t paying off in DC
articles.summary: A House Judiciary Committee report accuses South Korea of targeting American firms with coercive investigations and excessive fines. The findings suggest Seoul's lobbying efforts in Washington have failed to resolve these trade disputes. The report highlights ongoing friction between the two economies. Republicans on the House Judiciary Committee released in July an interim staff report accusing South Korea of “discriminatory attacks on American-owned businesses.” Seoul’s “practices include coercive investigation tactics, overly burdensome regulatory requirements, and massive fines and penalties intended to punish American businesses and make it harder for them to effectively compete against Kor.

articles.title: Scorched earth isn’t driving Ukrainians to sue for peace
articles.summary: Vladimir Putin believes relentless bombing of Ukrainian cities will force Kyiv to sue for peace. This marks his latest shifting theory of victory after earlier land offensives stalled. Polling data suggests this scorched earth strategy is not actually driving Ukrainians toward accepting a negotiated settlement. Vladimir Putin has a theory of victory in Ukraine. It’s not the Russian president’s first theory – that was a quick, dayslong campaign – nor his second or third, which involved different land offensives in the east that quickly petered out.

articles.title: Why Russia's Central Crimean Drone Base Is Hard For Ukraine To Destroy
articles.summary: Satellite imagery reveals a military airfield in central Crimea now functions as a primary hub for Russian drone launches. A Crimean military insider told RFE/RL that the site’s dispersed layout makes it difficult for Ukrainian forces to target effectively. The base uses multiple, smaller launch pads rather than a single concentrated runway. This fragmentation reduces the impact of any single precision strike. Ukraine has struggled to neutralize the facility despite repeated attempts. The infrastructure remains operational and continues to support Russian drone operations against Ukrainian targets.

articles.title: 'Committed To European Integration': Student List's Srdanovic On Serbia's Post-Vucic Future
articles.summary: Ilija Srdanovic, the lead candidate for Serbia’s Student List, confirmed the party’s commitment to European integration following Aleksandar Vucic’s defeat. The student-led opposition movement secured victory, ending over a decade of Vucic’s political dominance. Srdanovic outlined the next steps for the country in an interview with RFE/RL’s Balkan Service. The transition marks a significant shift in Serbian political leadership. Aleksandar Vucic’s election defeat has ended more than a decade of political dominance and handed victory to Serbia’s student-led opposition movement.

articles.title: Serbia Student List Lead Candidate Vows EU Integration, Open Debate On Russia Ties
articles.summary: Ilija Srdanovic leads Serbia's Student List party. The group recently ousted Aleksandar Vucic in elections. Srdanovic pledged to pursue EU integration. He also proposed a public debate on reconsidering sanctions against Russia. In an interview with RFE/RL, Ilija Srdanovic, the lead candidate for Serbia's Student List -- which ousted longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic in recent elections -- pledged to pursue EU integration and said Belgrade's stance on sanctions against Russia could be reconsidered through public debate.

articles.title: 'Get Killed Or Starve': Life Under Russian Occupation In Oleshky
articles.summary: Residents of Russian-occupied Oleshky face severe food shortages and threats. Civilians risk mines and drone attacks to escape the area. A proposed cease-fire could open a humanitarian corridor. This would allow trapped civilians to leave the Ukrainian city. Residents fleeing Russian-occupied Oleshky describe hunger, soaring food prices, and threats from Russian soldiers. Cut off from supplies, civilians risk mines and drone attacks to escape.

articles.title: General Assembly weighs US embargo against Cuba ahead of 34th vote
articles.summary: The United Nations General Assembly began its annual debate on the US economic embargo against Cuba. Member states will vote on Wednesday, 28 October, to end the sanctions. This will be the 34th consecutive annual resolution calling for the immediate termination of the trade restrictions. The General Assembly opened its annual debate on the US economic embargo against Cuba on Tuesday.

articles.title: Record carbon dioxide levels will impact us for centuries, says UN weather agency
articles.summary: The World Meteorological Organization reported that carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases hit record highs in 2025. Burning fossil fuels drove these levels, locking in additional long-term global warming. The agency warned these atmospheric changes will affect the planet for centuries. Levels of carbon dioxide (CO2) and other major greenhouse gases in the atmosphere caused by burning fossil fuels reached record highs in 2025, locking in more long-term global warming, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: Chinese markets lose trillions as race for AI supremacy with US takes its toll
articles.summary: Chinese stock markets lost trillions of dollars recently. Investors worry about the sustainability of Beijing’s AI boom. The race for supremacy against the United States is straining profits and raising concerns about the sector’s future. Lack of profits and the threat posed by western countries are raising concern about the sustainability of Beijing’s AI boomTrillions of dollars have been wiped from China’s stock markets in recent months amid increasing anxiety about the future of artificial intelligence, as Beijing races against the United States for dominance in the sector. articles.title: Cease-Fire in Ukraine's Oleshky Expanded To Help Flow Of Aid, Safe Passage
articles.summary: Russian air strikes hit Kyiv on October 26, targeting a university dormitory and other civilian buildings. At least one person died in the attacks. President Zelenskyy urged international partners to supply Ukraine with adequate defensive capabilities. Russian air attacks struck Kyiv late on October 26, hitting a university dormitory and other civilian sites, leaving at least one dead, as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called on Ukraine's partners to provide the "proper tools" for the country to defend itself.

articles.title: What Now For Serbia After Vucic's Stunning Election Defeat?
articles.summary: Aleksandar Vucic lost the Serbian parliamentary elections to student-led opposition. The ruling party was ousted from power. The new government must now navigate complex relations with the European Union, Russia, and China. Who will lead the next government of Serbia, after Aleksandar Vucic lost parliamentary elections, can the protest movement turn electoral success into stable rule, and what the result could mean for Serbia’s balancing relations with the European Union, Russia, and China?

articles.title: Iran, Regional Countries Agree To Continue Talks After Tehran Meeting
articles.summary: Mecca Defense Alliance partners met in Tehran to address regional conflicts. The snap meeting focused on stabilizing the Middle East. These tensions are currently disrupting global oil and cargo flows across the region. Officials from the so-called Mecca Defense Alliance have gathered for a snap meeting in Tehran as they look to settle conflicts in the Middle East that have left the region reeling and are impacting global flows of oil and other cargo.

articles.title: Investigators find Russia committed war crimes by targeting civilians
articles.summary: A panel of human rights experts concluded that Russian forces committed war crimes and crimes against humanity during the Ukraine invasion. The findings cite deliberate attacks on civilians and vital energy infrastructure. These actions violate international law. The report details specific violations of protected targets. Top human rights experts investigating Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine said on Monday that the Russian authorities had committed war crimes and crimes against humanity by attacking civilians and vital energy infrastructure, among other violations of international law.

articles.title: Women and girls’ share of civilian war deaths doubles since 2021
articles.summary: The United Nations reported that women and girls accounted for one in four of the more than 37,000 civilians killed in armed conflict last year. This figure represents a doubling of their share compared to 2021. The data highlights a significant shift in the demographic impact of global wars. Civilian casualties have risen sharply during this period. War is growing deadlier for women and girls, who accounted for one in four of the more than 37,000 civilians killed in armed conflict last year – double their share in 2021 – according to major UN report released Monday.

articles.title: US forces accused of ‘weaponising’ Somalia’s floods by trapping women and children in the path of
articles.summary: US airstrikes in southern Somalia are pushing civilians toward the rising River Juba. Women and children face drowning risks as they flee al-Shabaab territory. Humanitarian groups accuse the military of weaponizing the flood crisis. The strategy traps vulnerable populations in dangerous waterways. Exclusive: Coordinated airstrikes on territory held by al-Shabaab are driving the civilian population to find refuge alongside a river where rising water levels are a threat to safety.

articles.title: Student-Led Opposition Celebrates In Serbia After Vucic Concedes Election Defeat
articles.summary: Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in Serbia's October 25 parliamentary elections. The student-led Students' List took a decisive lead in preliminary results. This ends his fourteen-year dominance of Serbian politics. Former President Aleksandar Vucic, who dominated Serbian politics for the past 14 years, conceded defeat in the country's parliamentary elections after polls closed on October 25. Preliminary results showed the movement called Students' List taking a decisive lead.

articles.title: Vucic Concedes Electoral Defeat, Setting Stage For New Era Of Serbian Politics, Relations With West
articles.summary: Vucic admitted defeat to the student-led protest movement in Serbia's parliamentary vote. His concession signals a potential shift toward European alignment. The new government may distance Serbia from Kremlin influence. Aleksandar Vucic, Serbia's former president and dominant political figure for more than a decade, conceded defeat to the student-led protest movement in the country's parliamentary elections, potentially ushering in a new era of politics more closely aligned with Europe and away from the Kremlin.

articles.title: Women ‘first to suffer’ under siege, first to step up as frontline responders in Sudan
articles.summary: Tahani Al-Numeiri in Khartoum mistook the initial explosions for wedding celebrations on 15 April 2023. The Rapid Support Forces had just opened fire on the army. Women in Sudan now serve as frontline responders during the siege. They face immediate danger while managing critical aid distribution. The conflict has forced them into roles previously held by men. Their work sustains communities under active bombardment.

articles.title: Will Trump Help Putin Win in Ukraine?
articles.summary: Crisis Group experts discussed the rift between Washington and Kyiv. They analyzed Russia’s intensifying attacks on Ukraine. European capitals are working to strengthen Ukraine while facing their own political and economic pressures. This week on Hold Your Fire!, Richard speaks with Crisis Group experts Lucian Kim, Stephen Pomper and Fabienne Hara about the latest rift between Washington and Kyiv, Russia’s intensifying attacks and European capitals’ efforts to strengthen Ukraine while themselves under pressure.

articles.title: हिंद-प्रशांत में शांति के लिए भारत और अमेरिका एकजुट, राजनाथ सिंह ने पीट हेगसेथ के साथ तय किया नया
articles.summary: सेबू में भारत और अमेरिका ने हिंद-प्रशांत में रणनीतिक साझेदारी मजबूत करने का संदेश दिया। रक्षा मंत्री राजनाथ सिंह और पीट हेगसेथ ने दस वर्षीय सहयोग ढांचे की समीक्षा की। India-US Defence Partnership: फिलीपींस के सेबू शहर में भारत और अमेरिका ने हिंद-प्रशांत क्षेत्र में रणनीतिक साझेदारी को लेकर बड़ा संदेश दिया है. रक्षा मंत्री राजनाथ सिंह ने अमेरिकी वॉर सेक्रेटरी पीट हेगसेथ के साथ उच्चस्तरीय द्विपक्षीय बैठक कर दोनों मुल्कों के 10 वर्षीय रक्षा सहयोग ढांचे की गहन समीक्षा की.

articles.summary: ट्रंप ने नेतन्याहू की चुनावी वापसी का श्रेय अपने समर्थन को दिया। हालांकि, शुरुआती आंकड़े स्पष्ट जीत की गारंटी नहीं देते। नेतन्याहू मजबूत दक्षिणपंथी सरकार बनाने की बात कर रहे हैं। Benjamin Netanyahu News: इजरायल की सियासत में चुनावी मुकाबला दिलचस्प मोड़ पर पहुंच गया है। प्रधानमंत्री बेंजामिन नेतन्याहू की सत्ता बचाने की कोशिशों के बीच अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप ने उनकी चुनावी वापसी का श्रेय अपने समर्थन को दिया है।

articles.summary: केंद्रीय मंत्री अश्विनी वैष्णव ने बताया कि मोबाइल PLI योजना के तहत 19,000 करोड़ रुपये दिए गए। इसके बावजूद मोबाइल उद्योग से 3.25 लाख करोड़ रुपये का कर वसूला गया। केंद्रीय मंत्री अश्विनी वैष्णव ने बताया कि सरकार ने मोबाइल उत्पादन-लिंक्ड प्रोत्साहन (PLI) के तहत 19,000 करोड़ रुपये देने के बावजूद मोबाइल उद्योग से 3.25 लाख करोड़ रुपये का कर एकत्र किया है।
